learning: If the restored run scores near 203 with oval progress at or above 0.85, the platform is stable and later changes can be attributed to the controller. If oval oscillation stays near 0.34 with max_error near 0.06, damping is the next controller lever, not geometry. If s-bend and slalom max_error stay at 0.061 to 0.063, bend exits are controller- or speed-limited and geometry should stop changing.
notes: Restores the iteration 3 best geometry and controller exactly, so this race is a clean known-good baseline. Only the geometry is restored from the iteration 6 narrowing; no gains are changed.
rationale: Iteration 3 is still the best raced design (203.20). Iteration 6 narrowed wheel_track to 0.085 m and scored 155.17, with oval progress falling from 0.87 to 0.70 and no change at the bend exits (s-bend max_error 0.0629, slalom 0.0610). The 0.085 m track is therefore rejected. Iterations 4 and 5 also showed that widening the outer pair to 0.05 m and using 12 mm footprints both cost progress. I restore the iteration 3 geometry exactly (five 16 mm sensors at x = -0.04, -0.02, 0, 0.02, 0.04 and y = 0.06; wheel_track 0.09; body 0.22 x 0.12 m; mass 0.5 kg; wheel radius 0.03 m). I also restore the iteration 3 controller exactly (kp 2.2, kd 0.30, ki 0, base_speed 1.2, weights [-2,-1,0,1,2], last_direction). Keeping the controller identical to the best run gives a clean baseline, so any score change in this race comes from the restored geometry and from race-to-race variation, not from new gains. Oval oscillation was 0.339 at this setting, and the iteration 4 softening (kp 2.0, kd 0.35) moved it only to 0.333, so I do not change the damping here. Expected result: a score near 203, oval progress at or above 0.85, and oval max_error near 0.06. Line loss should stay at or below 1.0 per run.
